statuses.evidence: Closed at source level only. Both migrations are pending and unapplied, and production has no live verification path (see F1). (1) Same-transaction obligation: an AFTER INSERT trigger on payment_verifications inserts a 'held' canonical outbox row inside the verification transaction (20261001040351 effects.sql:187-217). The guard refuses any insert that is not 'held' or not exactly bound (effects.sql:154-172). Deleting or truncating bound rows is refused (effects.sql:98-104,126-131). The provider path inserts the verification inside settlement_commit, and a deferred guard requires the held outbox row (20261001115512:266-271,396-404,140-147). (2) Audit before notification: held may move only to pending, and only once a bound canonical audit receipt exists (effects.sql:144-151). The worker rechecks right before delivery (outbox.ts:251-256 -> payment-effects.ts:158-177 -> effects.sql:299-312). (3) Recovery works from stored facts only. It never reads the verifier grants (effects.sql:219-247,266-297; payment-effects.ts:75-105). It runs in the existing outbox worker tick (outbox.ts:588-595) and can also be started by admin drain/retry (outbox.ts:712-717,749-790) or by the verify/settle routes (http.ts:441-455,497-512). A receipt is read before preparing a fresh alias, so a key rotation or a concurrent completion converges (payment-effects.ts:82-103; effects.sql:277-290). Replays are idempotent: the outbox row is locked FOR UPDATE, the audit append dedupes on an advisory lock (effects.sql:273-296; audit_store.sql:331-393). (4) A failed completion only rolls back its own transaction. The verification is immutable and the outbox FK is ON DELETE RESTRICT (effects.sql:47-48). (5) Composition: finance is built only when resolvePaymentEffectsRecovery succeeds, and that requires a branded resolved durable audit authority plus the exact effects authority RPC (index.ts:1009-1023; payment-effects.ts:143-155). Settlement also requires effects (index.ts:1069). recordPaymentVerificationEffects is removed from service.ts. ADP03 changes only the method predicate, via an exactly-once string replacement (20261001115512:437-449), and makes the inherited effects triggers ENABLE ALWAYS (20261001115512:516-522). Residual P3 gaps are listed under findings.

findings.repro: Settle a provider capture while the audit is conflicting or recovery is disabled. financial_eligibility returns fulfillmentEligible=true, and paid->supplier_processing succeeds while the paid audit is absent.

findings.claim: The governed no-funds path is only required when a payment observation exists. A payment-stage request with an accepted quote and no recorded observation can still be cancelled with an admin free-text reason and customer message. In production observations cannot be recorded (manual evidence adapter null), so every real cancellation of payment_pending or payment_review skips N2. The reserved-copy guard matches only one exact sentence.

findings.claim: Assisted orders have no refund, void, partial refund, dispute or chargeback authority, in SQL or mounted runtime. Refund and dispute facts are only quarantined or held. Refund intent versus completion exists only as interface comments. A verified or provider-settled request cannot be cancelled or reversed at all. The only refund() code is a pre-existing, unmounted in-memory engine that records a completed refund from admin free-text reason and evidenceRef, allows one refund only, and has no intent/completion split.

findings.correction: Design a refund/void ledger: refund intent bound to verification and amount with an aggregate cap and partial refunds, then completion only from independent provider or bank evidence. Add dispute and chargeback states that freeze fulfillment without touching the verification, and a separate disposition kind with customer copy for each.
findings.repro: Verified manual payment (status paid). There is no RPC or route to record a refund. Ordinary cancel is refused by the observed_cancel_guard, and the no-funds graph refuses because a verification exists (062651:127).

findings.claim: Cross-lens, latent until a provider source is configured. A single unbound provider journal row (unknown_attempt, binding_mismatch, missing_event_identity, source_revoked or identity conflict) leaves established_request_id null. That permanently blocks quote issue and accept, every cancellation and every no-funds context or commit for ALL requests. Any provider attempt on a request permanently blocks its cancellation and no-funds resolution, even if the session expired unpaid. Journal and attempts are immutable, and there is no quarantine-resolution or provider no-funds path.

findings.correction: Scope the uncertainty to the requests an event can actually affect. Add a governed, append-only quarantine-resolution record. Add a provider no-funds disposition (failed or expired session, with retrieveAttempt evidence) so abandoned attempts can be cancelled.
findings.repro: With one configured source, append an authenticated event whose claimedAttemptId matches no attempt. After that, research_assisted_order_quote_issue on any unrelated reviewing request raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD through the aaa_adp01_uncertainty trigger.

findings.claim: Observation writes do not bind quote_id to the request's accepted quote (it comes from the browser body) and do not bound observed_at to now. Corrections inherit the original quote_id. The no-funds graph refuses any observation or correction on a non-accepted quote, and a receipt must postdate max(observed_at) while being no later than now. One mis-keyed observation therefore makes the request permanently impossible to cancel, verify or resolve as no-funds. This fails closed, but there is no recovery path.
findings.citation: 20260930234614:59-147 (observe has no quote/request/accepted check and no observed_at upper bound); finance.ts:180 (quoteId from body); 20260930230541:301-304,342 (correction keeps v_old.quote_id); 062651:134-140,149-154 (graph refusals), 293-301 and 413-420 (checked_at >= max(observed_at)), 278 (checked_at <= now); 062651:349-364 (cancel blocked).
findings.correction: In observe, require quote_id to be the request's current accepted quote and observed_at <= clock_timestamp(). Provide a governed void-observation disposition for mis-keyed evidence.

findings.claim: After a no-funds disposition, the terminal guard forbids any new observation, claim, correction, verification or quote for the request, and the customer has already been told no funds were received. Money that arrives after a 'terminal never_received' check cannot be recorded or returned in the system. checkedAt also has no maximum age: a receipt checked long before commit is accepted as long as it postdates the last graph write.
findings.citation: 062651:327-348 and 379-388 (aa_hl12_disposition_terminal on observations, verifications, corrections, claims, quotes); 062651:299-301 (only a lower bound against graph writes) and 278 (upper bound now); financial-disposition.ts:16-17,144-147 (no freshness check); 062651:315 and 551-552 (fixed customer copy).
findings.correction: Add a maximum receipt age relative to commit. Define a governed late-receipt path for post-disposition funds (record, then refund) that does not reopen the order.

findings.claim: There is no separation of duties: the same auth user can hold a payment-verifier grant (record the observation) and a no-funds grant (declare never received). Nothing checks that the resolver differs from the observer, corrector or verifier in the graph.

findings.claim: If the commit response is lost and the admin retries, context returns existingDispositionId but the service still calls the adapter and commit again. A fresh adapter receipt (new sourceReceiptId or checkedAt) changes the idempotency key and receipt, so SQL raises REPLAY_CONFLICT. The UI reports 'financial_disposition_refused' even though the cancellation committed.

verdict.reasoning:
The finding describes the code correctly, but it does not show a new P2 defect at 8f24082.

What is accurate:
- service.ts:859-865 refuses a cancellation only when the financial state is missing, there is an observation, the payment is verified, or the status is supplier_processing.
- The SQL guard at 20261001062651:349-364 checks observations only.
- 20260930191323:37-38 allows payment_pending/payment_review -> cancelled.
- The reserved-copy matches at 062651:110-113 and disposition-effects.ts:148-150 test one exact sentence.
- 062651:455-458 leaves events.customer_message unguarded when no disposition exists.
- server/index.ts:1022 and :1039 both pass null evidence adapters.

Why this is not P2:
1. The delta did not introduce it. At the previously reviewed core 61853e2, service.ts:860-861 has the same predicate, and 20260930230541:376-387 already installed the same observation-only hl12_observed_cancel guard. The prior review saw this boundary and scoped N2 to observed money. The new migration only adds the disposition clause.
2. The only real-money scenario is staff taking funds outside the system, which the system then cannot record. That is the root cause of the open F1 P1 (no independent manual evidence source), restated.
3. In system state, an accepted quote in a payment-stage status is not financial exposure at this SHA:
   - CustomerQuotePanel.tsx:115, 119 and 125 tell the customer that acceptance is not payment and "Do not send funds based on this quote."
   - The payment_pending copy says the same (service.ts:258, payment-status-copy.ts:11, 13).
   - No payment instructions are issued, and no table stores customer payment claims (the full list of assisted-order tables shows none).
   - paid cannot be reached through the admin path (service.ts:204-218 always throws).

The reserved-copy check is an anti-forgery guard on the canonical notice's identity (062651:513-523 and 545-557), not a content filter. Free-text customerMessage is a general capability of any manage-level admin on every status change (service.ts:880, 886). The disposition graph does not require any observations (062651:125-140), and contextSchema accepts an empty observations array (financial-disposition.ts:25-30). verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this at 8f24082 and could not. Every factual claim holds.

1) SQL has no refund or void authority.
- The disposition table allows only `kind text not null check(kind='no_funds')` (20261001062651:82).
- The authority object lists unsupportedKinds void and refund (062651:687-692). The migration header says "No void, refund, provider or historical-paid adoption" (062651:2).
- The shared type holds void, refund, provider and historical_paid (shared/research/assisted-order/financial-disposition.ts:7-8). The receipt is fixed to kind "no_funds" (line 13).

2) No mounted route exists. The route list in server/research/assisted-order/http.ts:235-536 covers quote, manual observation and verify (431, 439), no-funds cancel (462), provider attempts and prepare (477, 488) and provider settle (499). None of them is a refund, void, dispute or chargeback route.

3) Refund and dispute facts are only quarantined or held.
- The journal accepts refunded and dispute_* kinds (085559:341).
- The classifier defaults the category to 'quarantined' (085559:382). It marks refunded, dispute_* and unknown as 'unsupported_financial_effect' (085559:413-415).
- The runtime schemas pin the flags: refundEnabled false (provider-journal.ts:44, provider-execution.ts:26) and refundPolicy record_and_hold_only_v1 (provider-journal.ts:51, provider-execution.ts:30). The SQL authority matches (085559:598; 115512:583, 592).

4) Refund intent and completion appear only in the adapter port.
- `requestRefund` and `requestCancellation` are interface signatures that return `{state:"pending"}`, with the comment "A request is not proof" (payment/provider-adapter.ts:81-92).
- Aggregate-cap and dispute-freeze rules exist only as a doc comment (110-112).
- `git diff --stat 61853e2 HEAD` on provider-adapter.ts, service.ts and ports.ts is empty, so these files are unchanged.

5) A verified or settled request cannot be cancelled.
- The paid_hold_guard, which no later migration redefines, refuses paid or supplier_processing to cancelled with ASSISTED_ORDER_REFUND_AUTHORITY_NOT_READY (20260930202413:562-566).
- observed_cancel_guard refuses cancellation when an observation exists without a no_funds disposition (062651:349-364).
- The no-funds graph refuses any request that has a verification or a paid event (062651:125-133).
- A provider-settled request may only move forward through fulfillment. Anything else raises PROVIDER_FULFILLMENT_HELD (115512:346-358).
- The app transition table in server/research/assisted-order/service.ts:102-103 still offers paid to cancelled and supplier_processing to cancelled. SQL refuses both, so cancel appears available but always fails.

6) The only refund() is unmounted and in-memory.
- service.ts:4-5 says it is "Deliberately NOT mounted". Outside tests, no file imports AssistedOrderPaymentService.
- The only repository implementation is InMemoryAssistedOrderPaymentRepository (payment/memory-repository.ts:20-21).
- refund() (service.ts:700-769) takes free-text reason and evidenceRef. It records a completed refund directly and returns early if a refund already exists (724-726), so only one refund is possible. There is no intent/completion split.

7) No other path covers assisted orders.
- The commerce refund engine (server/research/commerce/refunds.ts, refund-executions.ts) works only on canonical orders.
- convertAcceptedAssistedRequest (server/research/orders/service.ts:85, 144) and conversion/gate.ts have no callers outside tests.
- AssistedRequestConversionPanel's "Record refund" button is never mounted.

Small corrections that do not change the verdict:
- Refund and dispute handling is more than "interface comments". There is a typed port, and the adapter checks the amount cap and adjustmentId on refunded and dispute events (provider-adapter.ts:206-207).
- On a provider-settled request, a later refunded or dispute event is linked to that request (085559:407, 447). This changes the settlement graph, so fulfillmentEligible turns false (115512:287-293, 353-358) and fulfillment freezes. That is a generic fail-closed hold, not a governed dispute state. It does not help manual-paid orders, and no mounted adapter can produce such events.

The gap is openly declared (N2 handoff line 79: "Void, refund, provider, historical-paid and post-fulfillment resolutions remain held"). It is the remaining part of N2 and should be tracked as that, not as a separate new P2. The severity stays P2 because a verified paid order that cannot be fulfilled has no governed refund, void or reversal at all.

verdict.reasoning:
I read the code at 8f24082 and every factual claim in the finding holds.

1. One unbound journal row puts every request on hold. In 20261001085559, line 225 checks `exists(... event_journal where established_request_id is null)` with no filter on the request, so `provider_uncertainty(p_request_id)` returns held='provider_unbound_event_held' whatever request is passed in. `assert_clear` (lines 234-243) raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD whenever held is not false. The same unscoped check is repeated in 20261001115512 at lines 287, 309 and 350, and in 20261001102904 at line 191.

2. Many classifications leave the request unbound. The classifier sets result_request/result_attempt only in the final else branch (085559:407). Conflict/event_identity_conflict (392), source_revoked (393), missing_event_identity (394), unknown_attempt (395), kind='unknown' (396), binding_mismatch (397-401) and payment_identity_conflict (402-405) all return a null request. The ADP02 wrapper adds one more null-request path for payment/session identity conflicts (102904:486-491). The rule `check((established_request_id is null)=(established_attempt_id is null))` (085559:149) makes these rows the global trigger.

3. The hold reaches the operations the finding names. The `aaa_adp01_uncertainty` trigger fires BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE on quotes (085559:550-552), and the final guard calls assert_clear on any quote write that changes the row (115512:366-368). That covers quote_issue's insert and supersede (20260930202413:342-344) and accept's update (20261001024018:165). Request status changes to cancelled, paid or any fulfillment status call assert_clear (115512:360-362). Inserts into no_funds_evidence and financial_dispositions also call assert_clear (115512:369-373). `disposition_graph`, which N2 context and commit use (062651:223,288,410,574), is wrapped to call assert_clear first (085559:492-498).

4. The project's own verification script demonstrates the global effect. supabase/verification/research_assisted_order_quote_provider_journal_local.mjs:430-450 appends unknown_attempt and binding_mismatch events. It then asserts that unrelated requests are refused with UNCERTAINTY_HELD: cancel on 721, no-funds context on 720, manual verify on 719, and paid->supplier_processing on 717. The HTTP harness (research_assisted_order_quote_provider_journal_http.ts:196-203) asserts the same hold on unrelated request 801. So the impact is wider than the finding states: manual payment verification and fulfillment progression for all requests are blocked too.

5. There is no way to clear it. Attempts, journal and fence are append-only: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE triggers raise ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_IMMUTABLE (085559:538), truncate is blocked (531), and all are ENABLE ALWAYS (532, 540). The attempt state column only allows 'held' (131). No migration adds a quarantine-resolution operation, and a git grep for quarantine/resolution/provider no-funds finds none. An attempt on a request holds that request permanently (085559:227-229). The settlement row exception admits only observations, verifications and claims for a full capture (115512:311-324), so a failed or expired session can never be cancelled or given a no-funds disposition. The shared type still lists 'provider' as a held disposition kind (shared/research/assisted-order/financial-disposition.ts:8).

Why it stays P2 rather than higher, and why it is not refuted:
- The global scope is a deliberate fail-closed design, and the gap is documented. The ADP01 handoff, lines 86-88, says the conservative global hold has no release or resolution operation in this foundation and must not be enabled operationally without the remaining workflow.
- It is latent today. Sources install empty (085559:4-5). Production composition passes a null source (payment/provider-journal.ts:96-97; handoff line 90). No external webhook route is mounted (handoff line 80).
- So there is no current production impact. But documenting the gap does not close it. Once a source is configured, a single misrouted, early or stale authenticated event (for example the 'early' or late-after-cancel cases at local.mjs:431 and 443) would halt all assisted-order financial work. That includes manual flows, and recovery would require a new schema migration.
- P2 latent matches the predecessor ADP-01 rating, of which this is the successor gap.

The proposed correction is reasonable: scope the uncertainty to the requests an event can actually affect, add an append-only governed quarantine resolution, and add a provider no-funds disposition backed by retrieved failed or expired session evidence.

findings.claim: Any single unbound provider journal row permanently freezes every financial transition on the whole platform, including manual-only orders that never touched a provider, and nothing can resolve it. The row can be a stray, misrouted, redelivered or post-revocation event. Severity is P2 while latent; it becomes P1 as soon as any source is configured.
findings.citation: Global check: provider_uncertainty reports held when any journal row has established_request_id null (085559:225-226). The same global check is in the settlement guard, eligibility and row_allowed (115512:199, 287, 309). Many classifications leave requestId null: source_revoked, missing_event_identity, unknown_attempt and kind='unknown' (085559:393-396), binding_mismatch (085559:397-401), and event or payment identity conflict (085559:390-392, 402-405). The ADP02 wrapper also nulls requestId on any session or payment binding mismatch, even for a known locked attempt (102904:486-491). The journal guard admits revoked sources: it checks scope but not revoked_at (085559:438-440). Runtime strips every claim from an event with the wrong scope, which persists it as a global hold (server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-journal.ts:172-177), and a malformed optional claim becomes kind 'unknown' (provider-journal.ts:178-185). Event fingerprint covers the raw-body payloadSha256 (provider-journal.ts:154,182; 085559:442), so a redelivery whose bytes differ conflicts. The hold reaches quotes insert/update, status changes, observations, verifications, claims, corrections, no-funds rows and dispositions (085559:542-555; 115512:360-373). Rows are immutable through ALWAYS triggers (085559:531-540), and there is no resolution function (git grep finds none). The harness confirms the hold applies to unrelated settled requests too (supabase/verification/research_assisted_order_quote_provider_settlement_local.mjs:268-277).
findings.correction: Bind any anomaly whose attempt the guard already locked to that request instead of nulling it. Reserve global holds for identity collisions across requests. Refuse, or dead-letter without blocking, events from revoked sources and events with the wrong account or mode. Fingerprint normalized semantic fields rather than the raw-body digest. Add a separately granted, append-only quarantine-disposition authority that can release the global fence with reviewed evidence. Do not let one stray event freeze manual finance.
findings.repro: Configure one source as DB owner. Through service_role, call provider_event_append with a valid envelope whose claimedAttemptId is null, or any event after setting the source's revoked_at. Then: provider_uncertainty(<any request>) returns held 'provider_unbound_event_held'. payment_observe for a manual-only request raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD. An admin quote insert or a customer quote accept on any request raises the same. Paid to supplier_processing on a settled request raises FULFILLMENT_HELD. Nothing can clear it.

findings.claim: Reserving a provider attempt, which makes no external call, freezes the request for good. It can never be cancelled, quoted again, paid manually or given a no-funds disposition. Attempts allow one per request, have a single 'held' state and are immutable. There is no abandon, expire or void, so a customer who simply abandons card checkout leaves the order stuck.
findings.citation: One attempt per request (085559:119) and state check(state='held') (085559:131). Any attempt makes the request held (085559:227-229). The guard on unsettled requests asserts clear on cancelled, paid and other transitions (115512:360-362), on quote insert/update (115512:366-368) and on dispositions and no-funds rows (115512:369-373). Immutable (085559:538-540). Reservation needs only status reviewing, payment_pending or payment_review plus an accepted quote (085559:262-275).
findings.correction: Add attempt terminal states (abandoned, expired, failed_closed) that a separately granted actor can enter with provider-retrieved evidence, for example a retrieve showing no succeeded charge and a cancelled payment intent. A terminal attempt releases the request-scoped hold while the journal is kept. Alternatively, defer reservation until the customer actually starts checkout and expire unused reservations.
findings.repro: Request R in payment_pending with an accepted quote. Call provider_attempt_reserve with a reservation-grant UUID, then do nothing. Admin PATCH status cancelled, the no-funds cancel, a quote reissue and manual payment_observe each raise ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD, now and forever.

findings.claim: Settlement only accepts a perfectly clean payment lifecycle. Normal events, including ADP02's own recovery path, make a captured payment permanently unsettleable while the request stays frozen (ADP-G2), so the customer is charged and the order can never progress. Cases: (a) any 'unknown' create result, even when ADP02's same-key re-create or a late response later binds the payment; (b) a claim left without a bound result after a process death; (c) a declined card followed by a successful retry, because the 'failed' event is bound; (d) a second 'captured' event, such as two provider event types mapped to captured; (e) a capture event without the session id that was bound at create, which ADP02 turns into a global conflict; (f) a webhook bound to the request before the payment identity binding forms, which pushes create_context into reconciliation_required forever, so the binding ADP03 requires never forms.
findings.citation: 115512:211-214 refuses settlement if any result is not bound or any claim lacks a bound result. ADP02 deliberately issues a second create claim inside the replay window after an unknown result (102904:182-196). The runtime timeout is 5 s and appends 'unknown' before the late object result (server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-execution.ts:153-154, 236-256). Settlement refuses any journal kind outside pending, authorized or captured, and any second captured event (115512:200-202). It requires a session match and a payment binding (115512:204-208). create_context goes to reconciliation_required on any journal row for the request (102904:191). The harness asserts these holds by design (settlement_local.mjs:109-118).
findings.correction: Make the settlement predicate tolerate the lifecycle: accept unknown create results that a later exact bound result for the same creation key supersedes; allow prior failed or pending events when exactly one captured event matches the binding; dedupe captures by provider payment id; treat a missing optional session id as non-conflicting. Add a governed reconciliation authority (retrieve-and-bind) for attempts in reconciliation_required. Until that exists, keep execution and settlement unconfigured.
findings.repro: Reserve, then prepare. The provider create takes more than 5 s, so an unknown result is appended. Once the lease expires, prepare again: same creation key, bound result, payment binding. A 'captured' webhook is journaled bound. settlement_commit then raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_SETTLEMENT_HELD from 115512:211-212, the request cannot be cancelled, and the money is captured.

findings.claim: After settlement, any new claim, result or journal row for the request changes the graph snapshot and blocks fulfillment for good, with no review authority. That includes a routine admin re-click of POST /provider-attempts/:attemptId/prepare, which create_context sends to 'retrieve' with no status or settlement gate, and benign out-of-order webhooks. The code comment says 'until reviewed', but no review path exists. A settled request also cannot be cancelled.
findings.citation: create_context returns 'retrieve' whenever a payment binding exists, before any status or global checks (102904:182-183). The claim guard accepts it (102904:224-225). The graph includes claims, results and journal rows (115512:103-108). Eligibility compares it to the snapshot (115512:288-293). The settled-request guard allows only the paid-to-closed chain plus eligibility (115512:345-358). The comment at 115512:90-92 says 'until reviewed'.

findings.claim: SQL cannot tell a provider-authentic fact from one typed by any service_role caller. Once a DB owner configures a source, a create policy, and reservation, execution and settlement grants, the service_role key alone can build a complete provider-paid chain with no provider and no human admin, ending in a paid status and a released 'Payment verified' email: reserve, claim, append an 'object' create result with a made-up providerPaymentId, append a 'captured' event, settle, complete effects. Every grant check compares a UUID the caller supplies itself. Nothing requires reservation, execution, settlement and verifier actors to be different people, and production has a single ADMIN_EMAIL identity. Journal authority v3 advertises 'authenticated_durable_evidence_only_v1', which overstates what SQL enforces. Today no path exists: sources, policies and grants install empty, no RPC creates them, and event_append refuses an unconfigured source. No HTTP path lets an admin type in a captured fact: the settle body must be {} and no ingress route is mounted.
findings.citation: Headers state JSON supplied through service_role is not proof (085559:3-4, 102904:3-4, 115512:4-5). event_append takes arbitrary normalized JSON (085559:459-468) and is granted to service_role (085559:607-612; 115512:531-541). Result append checks no grant or lease (102904:330-331, 441-456). Grants are looked up by p_actor_auth_user_id (085559:306-308; 102904:169-171; 115512:174-176). The settlement guard has no distinct-actor check (115512:150-228). The label is at 115512:582-583. Empty-config refusal is at 085559:438-440. The admin identity comes from requireSupabaseAdmin and ADMIN_EMAIL (server/research/assisted-order/express.ts:190-207). The settle command schema is {} (server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-settlement.ts:18,73), and only path params are passed (server/research/assisted-order/http.ts:496-515).
findings.correction: Bind provider authenticity to something only the ingress holds. One option: SQL verifies the provider signature over stored raw-body digest and timestamp with a Vault-held secret inside a SECURITY DEFINER function. Another: append runs as a dedicated ingestion DB role or JWT claim that the general server's service_role key does not have. Bind actor grants to a verified user JWT (auth.uid()) rather than a parameter. Enforce distinct auth_user_ids for reservation or execution versus settlement. Rename the authority label so it does not claim authentication SQL does not perform.
findings.repro: Seed one source, a create policy and the three grants as owner. Then, as service_role only: provider_attempt_reserve; provider_create_claim; provider_create_result_append with outcome 'object' and providerPaymentId 'pi_forged'; set the request to payment_review; provider_event_append with kind 'captured', the matching claimed ids, amount = quote total and a recent occurredAt; provider_settlement_commit with the settlement-grant UUID. The request becomes paid with a held outbox row, and payment_effects_complete releases the email.

findings.claim: Execution can be configured without event ingress. AssistedProviderJournalService.receiveAuthenticated has no mounted caller. Wiring a real execution source without a journal ingress route would create real provider payments whose captures can never be journaled or settled, freezing those requests (ADP-G2).

findings.claim: Settlement is atomic. One SECURITY DEFINER call inserts the settlement, then the observation (whose BEFORE trigger writes the evidence claim), then the verification (whose AFTER trigger writes the held outbox row), then set_status (paid status plus paid event). A deferred ALWAYS constraint trigger requires the complete graph at commit. The settlement facts are derived by the database, and caller-supplied derived fields are refused.

verified.claim: Any single unbound provider journal row permanently freezes every financial transition on the whole platform, including manual-only orders that never touched a provider, and nothing can resolve it. The row can be a stray, misrouted, redelivered or post-revocation event. Severity is P2 while latent; it becomes P1 as soon as any source is configured.
verified.citation: Global check: provider_uncertainty reports held when any journal row has established_request_id null (085559:225-226). The same global check is in the settlement guard, eligibility and row_allowed (115512:199, 287, 309). Many classifications leave requestId null: source_revoked, missing_event_identity, unknown_attempt and kind='unknown' (085559:393-396), binding_mismatch (085559:397-401), and event or payment identity conflict (085559:390-392, 402-405). The ADP02 wrapper also nulls requestId on any session or payment binding mismatch, even for a known locked attempt (102904:486-491). The journal guard admits revoked sources: it checks scope but not revoked_at (085559:438-440). Runtime strips every claim from an event with the wrong scope, which persists it as a global hold (server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-journal.ts:172-177), and a malformed optional claim becomes kind 'unknown' (provider-journal.ts:178-185). Event fingerprint covers the raw-body payloadSha256 (provider-journal.ts:154,182; 085559:442), so a redelivery whose bytes differ conflicts. The hold reaches quotes insert/update, status changes, observations, verifications, claims, corrections, no-funds rows and dispositions (085559:542-555; 115512:360-373). Rows are immutable through ALWAYS triggers (085559:531-540), and there is no resolution function (git grep finds none). The harness confirms the hold applies to unrelated settled requests too (supabase/verification/research_assisted_order_quote_provider_settlement_local.mjs:268-277).
verified.correction: Bind any anomaly whose attempt the guard already locked to that request instead of nulling it. Reserve global holds for identity collisions across requests. Refuse, or dead-letter without blocking, events from revoked sources and events with the wrong account or mode. Fingerprint normalized semantic fields rather than the raw-body digest. Add a separately granted, append-only quarantine-disposition authority that can release the global fence with reviewed evidence. Do not let one stray event freeze manual finance.
verified.repro: Configure one source as DB owner. Through service_role, call provider_event_append with a valid envelope whose claimedAttemptId is null, or any event after setting the source's revoked_at. Then: provider_uncertainty(<any request>) returns held 'provider_unbound_event_held'. payment_observe for a manual-only request raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD. An admin quote insert or a customer quote accept on any request raises the same. Paid to supplier_processing on a settled request raises FULFILLMENT_HELD. Nothing can clear it.

verdict.reasoning:
I read every cited location at 8f24082, and each one says what the finding claims.

**One unbound row holds every request**
- 20261001085559 lines 225-226: `provider_uncertainty` returns 'provider_unbound_event_held' for any request as soon as any journal row has `established_request_id is null`.
- 115512 has the same global check in three places: the settlement guard (199), `financial_eligibility` (287) and `row_allowed` (309). The settlement financial guard repeats it at 350, and the create-claim guard has it at 102904:191.
- No later migration replaces `provider_uncertainty`.

**The hold reaches all financial writes, including manual-only ones**
- Triggers on no_funds, dispositions, verifications, observations, claims and corrections, plus quote insert/update and request status changes, are installed at 085559:542-555. All are ENABLE ALWAYS.
- The 115512 `financial_guard` (338-377) sends manual rows through `row_allowed`, which returns false when no settlement exists, and then on to `assert_clear`. So with no settlement, manual observations, quote insert/accept and moves into paid/cancelled/fulfillment all raise UNCERTAINTY_HELD. Because cancellation is in that set, no request can even be cancelled.

**Many classifications leave the request unbound**
- In the classifier (085559:390-405), these outcomes all leave `result_request` null: event_identity_conflict, source_revoked, missing_event_identity, unknown_attempt, kind='unknown' (reason unsupported_financial_effect), binding_mismatch and payment_identity_conflict.
- kind='unknown' and binding_mismatch stay null even when the guard has already found and locked the attempt's request (435).
- The ADP02 wrapper (102904:486-491) returns requestId null on any session or payment binding mismatch for a locked attempt.

**Revoked sources and wrong scope**
- The journal guard (085559:438-440) checks scope but not revoked_at. `scope_valid` (194-199) ignores revocation too, so events from a revoked source are journaled as source_revoked and become a global hold.
- Runtime (provider-journal.ts:172-177) replaces claims with {} when scope is wrong. That makes `claimedAttemptId` null and kind 'unknown' (185), so the event lands as unknown_attempt.
- A malformed optional claim also forces kind 'unknown' (178-185).

**Redelivered events**
- The fingerprint is the digest of the whole normalized event, including payloadSha256 (provider-journal.ts:182; 085559:386, 442).
- So the same eventId arriving with different raw bytes becomes event_identity_conflict, which is unbound. Whether a given provider actually resends different bytes is provider-specific and not proven.

**Nothing governed can clear it**
- Journal rows are blocked from UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE by ALWAYS triggers (085559:531-540).
- The granted RPCs are reserve, append, uncertainty and authority only (607-611), and no migration up to the tip adds a resolution path.
- The ADP01 handoff (.xenios/handoffs/2026-10-01T10-26-46-556Z-...ADP01...md:86-88) says it directly: "This conservative global hold has no release/resolution operation in this foundation."
- The harness seeds the global unbound event last and asserts FULFILLMENT_HELD on an already-settled request (settlement_local.mjs:269-277), which matches the claim that the freeze reaches unrelated requests.

**Severity**
P2 latent is right; I would not raise it now. The migrations are pending. Sources install empty (085559:4-5), and nothing outside the verification harnesses inserts one. Production wiring passes `source: null` (server/index.ts:1054, 1062, 1071). The finding's "P1 once configured" is a conditional and fair: with a real provider account, any authenticated event that matches no attempt would freeze all manual finance permanently, for example a dashboard-created payment or an account-wide webhook.
verdict.counterEvidence:
- The gap is documented. The ADP01 handoff (lines 86-88) says the global hold has no release or resolution operation and "must not be enabled operationally without the remaining workflow."
- The design is deliberately fail-closed. The comment at 085559:113-114 says unknown events lock only the fence and never a request. Keeping post-revocation evidence instead of discarding it is also intentional (handoff line 109: "revocation cannot clear holds").
- It is fully latent today: the migrations are pending, sources install empty, production passes a null source, and no non-test seed exists.
- A superuser could still remove a row by disabling the ALWAYS triggers. That is ungoverned break-glass, so "nothing can resolve it" is slightly overstated, but no governed path exists.
- The byte-different redelivery case is plausible but depends on how a particular provider resends events.
None of these refute the defect. They support keeping it at P2 latent rather than P1 now.

verified.claim: Reserving a provider attempt, which makes no external call, freezes the request for good. It can never be cancelled, quoted again, paid manually or given a no-funds disposition. Attempts allow one per request, have a single 'held' state and are immutable. There is no abandon, expire or void, so a customer who simply abandons card checkout leaves the order stuck.
verified.citation: One attempt per request (085559:119) and state check(state='held') (085559:131). Any attempt makes the request held (085559:227-229). The guard on unsettled requests asserts clear on cancelled, paid and other transitions (115512:360-362), on quote insert/update (115512:366-368) and on dispositions and no-funds rows (115512:369-373). Immutable (085559:538-540). Reservation needs only status reviewing, payment_pending or payment_review plus an accepted quote (085559:262-275).
verified.correction: Add attempt terminal states (abandoned, expired, failed_closed) that a separately granted actor can enter with provider-retrieved evidence, for example a retrieve showing no succeeded charge and a cancelled payment intent. A terminal attempt releases the request-scoped hold while the journal is kept. Alternatively, defer reservation until the customer actually starts checkout and expire unused reservations.
verified.repro: Request R in payment_pending with an accepted quote. Call provider_attempt_reserve with a reservation-grant UUID, then do nothing. Admin PATCH status cancelled, the no-funds cancel, a quote reissue and manual payment_observe each raise ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD, now and forever.

verdict.adjustedSeverity: P2-latent (activation blocker; cannot be reached in any composition at 8f24082)
verdict.reasoning:
The mechanism is real at 8f24082, but the finding overstates how reachable it is, and the gap is already documented.

What the code confirms (all at 8f24082):
- One attempt per request: `request_id ... unique` (20261001085559:119). The only state is held: `state ... check(state='held')` (085559:131).
- Attempts cannot be changed or deleted. `adp01_immutable` blocks update and delete on `research_assisted_order_provider_attempts`, and it is enabled always (085559:526-540).
- `provider_uncertainty` returns `provider_attempt_held` whenever any attempt row exists for the request (085559:227-229). `assert_clear` raises `ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_UNCERTAINTY_HELD` in that case (085559:238-241).
- The replaced financial guard calls `assert_clear` in four places:
  - status changes to cancelled, paid or closed (20261001115512:360-362, trigger at 085559:553-555)
  - quote insert or update, which covers reissue (115512:366-368, trigger at 085559:550-552)
  - inserts into observations, claims, verifications, dispositions and no-funds evidence. With no settlement row, `row_allowed` returns false (115512:307-308), so the guard falls through to `assert_clear` (115512:369-373). The triggers are at 085559:542-547.
- The `disposition_graph` wrapper also asserts clear (085559:492-497).
- Reservation needs only a status of reviewing, payment_pending or payment_review, plus an exact accepted quote (085559:261-275).
- Nothing in 085559, 102904 or 115512 adds an abandon, expire, void or release path. 115512:3 lists void and refund as non-goals.
- The ADP02 create context only reports `reconciliation_required` or `wait` (102904:182-196). It never releases the attempt.

So once a reservation exists, the request can never be cancelled, closed, requoted, paid manually or given a no-funds disposition. The finding's mechanism and repro are correct at the SQL level.

Why I downgrade it:
1. It is latent and cannot be reached.
   - Production passes `source: null` unconditionally (server/index.ts:1050-1055).
   - `buildAssistedProviderJournal` returns null without a valid source (payment/provider-journal.ts:223-228), so the route is mounted as `assistedOrderUnavailableDoor` (server/index.ts:1146-1149).
   - Even with a source, `reserveHeld` throws "Card payments are not configured" before any RPC (provider-journal.ts:117).
   - In SQL, sources and grants install empty (085559:1-6), service_role has no table privileges on them (085559:530, 618-625), and only reserve, append, uncertainty and authority are executable (085559:607-612). The repro therefore needs owner-level provisioning of a source and a reservation grant, and all seven migrations are still pending.
2. The scenario is wrong about who reserves. There is no customer card checkout to abandon. Reservation is an admin-only POST (http.ts:474-482; provider-journal.ts:110-112). The abandonment case describes a future flow that does not exist yet.
3. The gap is already declared. The ADP01 handoff says the hold "has no release/resolution operation in this foundation" and "must not be enabled operationally without the remaining workflow" (handoff 2026-10-01T10-26-46, lines 83-88), and lists void and resolution as separate work (356-358). The ADP02 handoff says "the attempt remains held for reconciliation" (2026-10-01T11-54-53, lines 93-95) and that "governed void/refund" remains engineering work (360-363). This overlaps the open N2 item (no governed void or refund) and the earlier ADP-01 latent line.

The finding still adds something worth keeping. ADP02 writes a create claim durably before any dispatch (102904:62-81, 250-284). That means an attempt with zero claims has provably made no external call, so a governed release of an unclaimed reservation would not need provider evidence. That is a narrower and safer correction than the proposed provider-retrieve terminal states, and it should be an explicit gate before the journal or execution flags or a source are ever enabled. Keep it as a P2-latent activation blocker linked to N2 and ADP-01, not as an active P2.
verdict.counterEvidence: The route cannot be reached in any composition. server/index.ts:1054 hard-codes `source: null`, buildAssistedProviderJournal returns null without a source (payment/provider-journal.ts:226-227), and the route falls back to assistedOrderUnavailableDoor (server/index.ts:1146-1149). reserveHeld refuses before any RPC when there is no source (provider-journal.ts:117). Provider sources and grants install empty and service_role cannot write them (085559:1-6, 530, 618-625), and the migrations are pending. Reservation is admin-initiated (http.ts:474-482), not a customer checkout step. The gap is documented as a known non-goal: the ADP01 handoff (lines 83-88) says the hold "has no release/resolution operation in this foundation" and must not be enabled operationally. The ADP02 handoff (93-95, 360-363) keeps attempts "held for reconciliation" with governed void/refund still open, and 115512:3 excludes void and refund. It overlaps the open N2 item and the ADP-01 latent line.

verified.claim: Settlement only accepts a perfectly clean payment lifecycle. Normal events, including ADP02's own recovery path, make a captured payment permanently unsettleable while the request stays frozen (ADP-G2), so the customer is charged and the order can never progress. Cases: (a) any 'unknown' create result, even when ADP02's same-key re-create or a late response later binds the payment; (b) a claim left without a bound result after a process death; (c) a declined card followed by a successful retry, because the 'failed' event is bound; (d) a second 'captured' event, such as two provider event types mapped to captured; (e) a capture event without the session id that was bound at create, which ADP02 turns into a global conflict; (f) a webhook bound to the request before the payment identity binding forms, which pushes create_context into reconciliation_required forever, so the binding ADP03 requires never forms.
verified.citation: 115512:211-214 refuses settlement if any result is not bound or any claim lacks a bound result. ADP02 deliberately issues a second create claim inside the replay window after an unknown result (102904:182-196). The runtime timeout is 5 s and appends 'unknown' before the late object result (server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-execution.ts:153-154, 236-256). Settlement refuses any journal kind outside pending, authorized or captured, and any second captured event (115512:200-202). It requires a session match and a payment binding (115512:204-208). create_context goes to reconciliation_required on any journal row for the request (102904:191). The harness asserts these holds by design (settlement_local.mjs:109-118).
verified.correction: Make the settlement predicate tolerate the lifecycle: accept unknown create results that a later exact bound result for the same creation key supersedes; allow prior failed or pending events when exactly one captured event matches the binding; dedupe captures by provider payment id; treat a missing optional session id as non-conflicting. Add a governed reconciliation authority (retrieve-and-bind) for attempts in reconciliation_required. Until that exists, keep execution and settlement unconfigured.
verified.repro: Reserve, then prepare. The provider create takes more than 5 s, so an unknown result is appended. Once the lease expires, prepare again: same creation key, bound result, payment binding. A 'captured' webhook is journaled bound. settlement_commit then raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_SETTLEMENT_HELD from 115512:211-212, the request cannot be cancelled, and the money is captured.

verdict.adjustedSeverity: P2-latent (blocks activation; cannot be reached at 8f24082, the same footing as ADP-01 "P2 latent")
verdict.reasoning:
The code does what the finding says. Every citation checks out at 8f24082. The stated impact, a customer charged with an order that can never progress, cannot happen at this SHA, so the finding is a latent design gap, not a live P2.

Confirmed mechanics:
- supabase/migrations/20261001115512_research_assisted_order_quote_provider_settlement.sql
  - Lines 211-212 refuse settlement if any create result for the attempt is not bound/exact_binding.
  - Lines 213-214 refuse settlement if any claim has no bound result.
  - Lines 200-202 refuse any journal row for the request that is not bound/exact_binding, whose kind is outside pending/authorized/captured, or that is a second captured row.
  - Lines 204-208 require a payment binding and an exact session match.
- supabase/migrations/20261001102904_research_assisted_order_quote_provider_execution.sql
  - Lines 182-196: once the lease expires and no payment binding exists, the context returns 'create' again inside the replay window. That is the same-key recovery path.
  - Lines 330-331 and 350: a late object result may still be appended to the original claim. Its fingerprint differs, so the earlier 'unknown' row stays.
- server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-execution.ts
  - Lines 153-154 cap the timeout at 5 s.
  - Lines 236-256 commit the timeout 'unknown' result first, then still append the late object result.
  - So even ADP02's best recovery case, a late response that binds, leaves an 'unknown' row, and 115512:211-212 then holds settlement permanently. This internal contradiction between ADP02 recovery and ADP03 settlement is real.
- The pre-execution classifier binds a webhook to a request using only claimedAttemptId metadata (085559:433-434 and 397-416), with no payment binding. The context then goes to reconciliation_required (102904:191).
- ADP02's classifier wrapper returns requestId null on a session mismatch, including a null session id (102904:486-491). That creates a global hold (115512:199, 115512:287, 085559:225).
- assert_clear refuses cancellation, manual verification and no-funds disposition for any request that has an attempt (085559:227, 085559:495, 115512:360-362 and 372-373). So the request really is frozen, and no reconciliation or retrieve-without-binding authority exists.
- The harness asserts these holds as designed (settlement_local.mjs:109-118).

Why this is a downgrade:
1. Nothing can be activated at this SHA. server/index.ts:1050-1072 builds the journal, execution and settlement services with `source: null`, so all three are null whatever the env flags say (provider-execution.ts:320-324). All three migrations are still pending. No create policy, execution grant, settlement policy or grant is seeded (102904:5, 115512:1-3). No adapter or SDK exists (provider-execution.ts:66-72). The REPRO's ">5 s provider create" and captured webhook therefore cannot occur, and no money can be captured.
2. The finding's own interim fix, "keep execution and settlement unconfigured", is already the state of the code.
3. The fail-closed hold is a documented intent. The ADP02 handoff (lines 93-95) says the attempt "remains held for reconciliation", and the ADP03 contract (handoff lines 43-45) is to "reject unsupported, ambiguous, unbound, stale and adverse facts".
4. The design gap remains: no reconciliation authority exists, and ADP02's recovery yields attempts ADP03 can never settle. It must be fixed before any activation.

Sub-case accuracy:
- Cases (a) and (b) follow directly from the SQL and runtime.
- Cases (c), (d) and (e) depend on how a future adapter normalizes events (decline then retry on the same payment, two event types mapped to captured, capture events without a session id). They are plausible, not shown.
- Case (f) is overstated. A late result can still bind after the webhook, and once payment_id exists the context returns 'retrieve' (102904:183, checked before 191). So "never forms" holds only when the original response is lost, for example after a process death. When the binding does form, case (a) still blocks settlement.

verified.claim: After settlement, any new claim, result or journal row for the request changes the graph snapshot and blocks fulfillment for good, with no review authority. That includes a routine admin re-click of POST /provider-attempts/:attemptId/prepare, which create_context sends to 'retrieve' with no status or settlement gate, and benign out-of-order webhooks. The code comment says 'until reviewed', but no review path exists. A settled request also cannot be cancelled.
verified.citation: create_context returns 'retrieve' whenever a payment binding exists, before any status or global checks (102904:182-183). The claim guard accepts it (102904:224-225). The graph includes claims, results and journal rows (115512:103-108). Eligibility compares it to the snapshot (115512:288-293). The settled-request guard allows only the paid-to-closed chain plus eligibility (115512:345-358). The comment at 115512:90-92 says 'until reviewed'.
verified.correction: Refuse new create or retrieve claims once a settlement exists, or exclude post-settlement retrieve facts from the eligibility graph. Add a separately granted, append-only 'graph reviewed' acknowledgement that re-baselines eligibility for benign facts while refunds and disputes stay held.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked every citation at 8f240828 and each one says what the finding claims.

1. **Prepare re-click becomes a 'retrieve' claim.** In create_context (20261001102904:182-183), a claim whose lease has expired falls through to `elsif payment_id is not null then next_action:='retrieve'`. That happens before the status and global checks at :184-195.
   - The checks that run earlier (source, policy and grant at :161-171; accepted quote at :172-176) all still pass after settlement. Settlement requires a payment binding (20261001115512:207). The quote cannot change, because adp03_evidence_immutable refuses updates on a settled request's quotes (115512:418-419, 474-483).
   - The claim guard accepts 'retrieve' (102904:224-225). Inserts into create_claims are checked only by adp02_claim and adp02_immutable (102904:497-520). No settlement guard is attached; the aaa_adp01_uncertainty financial guard is not on that table (085559:542-555).
   - The runtime adds no gate either. prepare() (provider-execution.ts:157-268) calls create_context, then create_claim, then the provider's retrieve, then result_append. The route (http.ts:485-493) has no status or settlement check.
2. **Any new row changes the snapshot.** The graph is the full to_jsonb of journal, claims, results and bindings (115512:103-108). The settlement snapshot is frozen at insert (:216, :225) and is immutable (:465-466).
3. **The hold is permanent.** Eligibility reports provider_uncertainty_held whenever the graph differs from the snapshot (115512:291-292). The financial guard allows only paid→supplier_processing→shipped→delivered→closed, and only when the request is eligible. Anything else raises ASSISTED_ORDER_PROVIDER_FULFILLMENT_HELD (:345-358).
   - Claims, results, journal rows and settlements are all update/delete-immutable, so nothing can bring the graph back to the snapshot.
   - No review or rebaseline authority exists. Searching migrations, server, shared and records for graph_snapshot, settlement_graph or any rebaseline/review mechanism finds only the comment at 115512:90-92.
4. **Benign webhooks.** A late pending or authorized event with a new eventId for the bound attempt is still classified 'bound' after settlement. The only terminal check is cancelled/closed status or a disposition (085559:408-416). The row gets established_request_id=r.id and changes the graph. An exact redelivery is deduplicated (085559:443-444).
5. **The repo reproduces this itself.** The local proof (supabase/verification/research_assisted_order_quote_provider_settlement_local.mjs:187-193) runs exactly this repro: settle, wait for the lease, claim gives nextAction 'retrieve', append, fulfillmentEligible=false, and paid→supplier_processing refused with FULFILLMENT_HELD.

**Why not P1, and why latent:**
- **It is deliberate and safe for money.** The eligibility policy is named 'reviewed_lineage_no_new_facts_v1' (115512:601; provider-settlement.ts:24), and the proof treats this hold as intended. No money moves incorrectly. The defect is liveness and governance: the comment promises "until reviewed", but no review authority exists. The system's own ungated admin action can strand a captured payment for good.
- **It is not reachable today.** The migrations are pending, and the SQL seeds no policies or grants. Startup passes `source: null` for both execution and settlement (server/index.ts:1058-1072), so the prepare and settle routes answer unavailable. No client code calls provider-attempts.

**Two refinements:**
- The "re-click" needs the previous lease to have expired. Inside the lease, the call returns 'wait' (102904:182), and lease_ms is at most 300 s.
- The "settled request cannot be cancelled" part (115512:354-358) is the same gap as open N2 (no governed void/refund). The handoff says so itself: a later refund keeps verification and holds progress, with no refund-resolution authority. That part should not count as a separate P2.

What is new beyond N2: benign facts, including the system's own retrieve, permanently block fulfillment with no gate and no rebaseline. That is consistent with how ADP-01 was rated (P2 latent), so P2 latent stands.

6. **The cancellation sub-claim overlaps open N2.** The ADP03 handoff, lines 357-362, already says there is no governed refund-resolution authority.

verified.claim: SQL cannot tell a provider-authentic fact from one typed by any service_role caller. Once a DB owner configures a source, a create policy, and reservation, execution and settlement grants, the service_role key alone can build a complete provider-paid chain with no provider and no human admin, ending in a paid status and a released 'Payment verified' email: reserve, claim, append an 'object' create result with a made-up providerPaymentId, append a 'captured' event, settle, complete effects. Every grant check compares a UUID the caller supplies itself. Nothing requires reservation, execution, settlement and verifier actors to be different people, and production has a single ADMIN_EMAIL identity. Journal authority v3 advertises 'authenticated_durable_evidence_only_v1', which overstates what SQL enforces. Today no path exists: sources, policies and grants install empty, no RPC creates them, and event_append refuses an unconfigured source. No HTTP path lets an admin type in a captured fact: the settle body must be {} and no ingress route is mounted.
verified.citation: Headers state JSON supplied through service_role is not proof (085559:3-4, 102904:3-4, 115512:4-5). event_append takes arbitrary normalized JSON (085559:459-468) and is granted to service_role (085559:607-612; 115512:531-541). Result append checks no grant or lease (102904:330-331, 441-456). Grants are looked up by p_actor_auth_user_id (085559:306-308; 102904:169-171; 115512:174-176). The settlement guard has no distinct-actor check (115512:150-228). The label is at 115512:582-583. Empty-config refusal is at 085559:438-440. The admin identity comes from requireSupabaseAdmin and ADMIN_EMAIL (server/research/assisted-order/express.ts:190-207). The settle command schema is {} (server/research/assisted-order/payment/provider-settlement.ts:18,73), and only path params are passed (server/research/assisted-order/http.ts:496-515).
verified.correction: Bind provider authenticity to something only the ingress holds. One option: SQL verifies the provider signature over stored raw-body digest and timestamp with a Vault-held secret inside a SECURITY DEFINER function. Another: append runs as a dedicated ingestion DB role or JWT claim that the general server's service_role key does not have. Bind actor grants to a verified user JWT (auth.uid()) rather than a parameter. Enforce distinct auth_user_ids for reservation or execution versus settlement. Rename the authority label so it does not claim authentication SQL does not perform.
verified.repro: Seed one source, a create policy and the three grants as owner. Then, as service_role only: provider_attempt_reserve; provider_create_claim; provider_create_result_append with outcome 'object' and providerPaymentId 'pi_forged'; set the request to payment_review; provider_event_append with kind 'captured', the matching claimed ids, amount = quote total and a recent occurredAt; provider_settlement_commit with the settlement-grant UUID. The request becomes paid with a held outbox row, and payment_effects_complete releases the email.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked every citation at 8f24082 and they are accurate. The repro chain would also work once someone configures it. Severity is the problem: this is a trust model the code documents, it cannot be reached today, and it adds no forgery capability that the existing manual path does not already give the same key holder.

What I confirmed at 8f24082:
- **Headers.** Each migration says service_role JSON is not proof: 085559:2-4 ("authenticated-adapter event quarantine", "SQL validates configured ingress, not external signatures"), 102904:3-4, and 115512:4-5 ("trusted integration boundary, not SQL cryptographic proof").
- **Event append.** event_append takes normalized JSON (085559:459-468) and is granted to service_role (085559:607-612; 115512:531-541, 610-611).
- **Result append.** It checks only that the issued claim exists and the source, scope and policy match; it checks no grant or lease (102904:330-331, 441-456).
- **Grant lookups.** All three key on a UUID parameter: 085559:306-308, 102904:169-171 and 244-245, 115512:174-176.
- **Distinct people.** Nothing compares the settlement actor with the reservation or execution actor (115512:150-228).
- **Repro step to payment_review.** set_status is granted to service_role (20260930191323:146), and payment_pending→payment_review is an allowed transition (191323:37).

Why P2 is too high:
1. **Unreachable today.** Sources, policies and grants install empty, and no RPC creates them. event_append refuses an unconfigured source (085559:438-440). Startup passes `source: null` to the journal, execution and settlement services (server/index.ts:1054, 1062, 1071), so all three build to null (provider-settlement.ts:99-104). The settle body must be `{}` (provider-settlement.ts:18, 73), and no ingress route calls event_append. The finding concedes all of this.
2. **No new capability.** The same service_role key can already forge a paid chain more easily through the manual path, which is mounted in production (index.ts:1140-1141):
   - payment_observe(method='manual') looks up the grant by a caller-supplied p_actor_auth_user_id (20260930234614:102-105).
   - verify_bound takes p_verifier_auth_user_id and requires the observer and verifier to be the same person (234614:188-192). It is granted to service_role (234614:262-269).
   - It moves the request to paid and writes the held F4 outbox row, and payment_effects_complete is service_role-callable (040351:266-297, 332).
   - That path needs one verifier-grant row. The provider path needs a source, a create policy, a settlement policy and three grants.

   So "caller-supplied UUID grants, no authenticity binding, no separation of duties, single ADMIN_EMAIL identity" is the existing F1 posture. F1 is already open as P1 ("no independent manual evidence source/grant procedure"). It is not new provider-specific exposure.
3. **No separation-of-duties claim.** Nothing in SQL or the handoff promises different people. The handoff says only that a separate grant table is needed: "reservation, execution, generic admin and manual-verifier grants do not suffice" (ADP03 handoff:40-41). The error text "Distinct settlement grant required" (115512:176) means the same thing. The manual path deliberately requires observer = verifier.
4. **Gap already disclosed and tracked.** The handoff says provider authentication is unproven: "not managed PostgREST/JWT or processor authentication" (ADP03 handoff:228-231) and "Provider authentication ... and activation are not proven" (handoff:365-366). ADP-01 (latent) already tracks the missing provider ingress authority.

What survives, at P3:
- **Label wording.** 'authenticated_durable_evidence_only_v1' (115512:582-583) can be read as SQL-enforced authentication, but its own header scopes it to adapter-authenticated ingress (085559:2-3). A rename or a clarifying comment would remove the ambiguity.
- **Activation precondition.** Before any source or grant is configured, provider ingress authenticity should be bound to something the general server's service_role does not hold, such as a dedicated ingest role or signature verification. Distinct-actor rules should be decided then too. This is a precondition to record against ADP-01/F1, not an independent P2 defect in the current source.
verdict.counterEvidence:
The provider path gives a service_role holder no forgery power it lacks today. The manual path's research_assisted_order_payment_observe (supabase/migrations/20260930234614_research_assisted_order_quote_provider_hold.sql:102-105) and verify_bound (234614:188-192, 262-269) are granted to service_role. Both trust a caller-supplied auth_user_id against payment_verifier_grants, and verify requires observer = verifier. The result reaches paid plus the held F4 outbox row, which service_role releases via payment_effects_complete (20261001040351:266-297, 332). This is the open F1 P1 posture, and the manual routes are mounted (server/index.ts:1140-1141).

The provider chain cannot run: startup passes `source: null` to all three services (server/index.ts:1054, 1062, 1071), the builders return null (provider-settlement.ts:99-104), the config tables install empty with no creating RPC, and event_append refuses an unconfigured source (085559:438-440).

The code states the trust boundary rather than hiding it: 085559:2-4, 102904:3-4, 115512:4-5, and ADP03 handoff lines 228-231 and 365-366. No source claims different people: "Distinct settlement grant required" (115512:176) and handoff:40-41 refer to a separate grant table, not a separate person.

verdict.reasoning:
I recomputed the hashes myself with LF normalization (`git show HEAD:<path> | tr -d '\r' | sha256sum`), and again from the clean worktree files on disk. Every cited value matched.
- `server/static.ts` hashes to `b7a76417…9f94`. The hard pin at `docs/phase2/CORE_SITE_PROTECTION_MANIFEST.json:703` is `9cd3e1c3…0004`.
- `client/src/App.tsx` hashes to `1bc59371…a57a7`. The seam pin at `:1254` is `3b3b808b…828d80`.
- `server/index.ts` hashes to `ba5800e6…4521`. The seam pin at `:1255` is `1d6594d6…c315`.
- `server/research/index.ts` hashes to `5b9f683b…4188`. The seam pin at `:1256` is `b8db03cf…3070`.
- `server/routes.ts` still matches its pin `7c21ea1a…`.

How the gate fails:
- `scripts/acceptance/verify-core-site-protection.mjs:302` checks `manifest.fileHashes.files` against the worktree. `:253-272` counts any `fileHashes` mismatch as a failure, so `main()` returns exit 1 (`:324`).
- This happens whatever the base ref is, because the hash check reads the worktree and does not use the diff. The `static.ts` mismatch alone gives "RESULT: FAIL".
- Two Vitest tests also fail: `server/core-site-protection.test.ts:319-324` (all `fileHashes` must match at HEAD, so `static.ts` fails it) and `:385-389` (all seam baselines must be clean, so App, index and research/index fail it).
- The manifest says every candidate "must pass scripts/acceptance/verify-core-site-protection.mjs before review". So 8f24082 cannot be released until an owner reviews and amends the pins.

Where the delta's changes came from:
- `git diff 61853e2 8f24082` changes `static.ts` and `App.tsx` by one line each. Both lines came from commit 0d22757, which removed the `/research/access-hub` redirect.
- `server/index.ts` gains 87 net lines across five HL-12 commits (3562c03, cb9b8d6, 5809b72, 27463d7, 2f0a975).
- The manifest is not touched in the delta.

The authors already know about the hold. HL17 doc lines 38-40 say "Any mismatch is a release hold, not an authorized baseline amendment", and the ADP03 handoff (around line 304) records `core-site-protection.test.ts:387` as the only failing test.

Corrections that do not change the verdict:
1. The finding says "a mismatch is an unconditional FAIL". That is true for `fileHashes` (`static.ts`). For seam baselines it is wrong as applied to the verifier: `verify-core-site-protection.mjs:240-244` labels them "reported, not a failure", and `:269-272` leaves them out of `failed`. The three seam mismatches fail only the Vitest assertion at `:385-389`.
2. The `server/research/index.ts` mismatch is older than this delta. At 61853e2 the file already hashed to `5b9f683b`, against the `b8db03cf` pin. Only the `static.ts`, `App.tsx` and `server/index.ts` mismatches are new in 61853e2..8f24082.
3. The `static.ts` and `App.tsx` changes are each a single-line redirect removal. Their behavior is not a defect.

P1 stands because the hard tripwire on `static.ts` alone makes the mandatory gate exit 1 at this SHA, which is a real release blocker. The proposed fix is sound: the owner amends the pins with reviewed comments, and the two HL-17 hashes wait for the SEAM-GOV-01 decision.
verdict.counterEvidence:
The finding is overstated in three places:
1. Seam-baseline mismatches are not an unconditional verifier failure. `scripts/acceptance/verify-core-site-protection.mjs:240-244` reports them as "reported, not a failure", and `:269-272` excludes them from `failed`. Only the Vitest test at `server/core-site-protection.test.ts:385-389` fails on them.
2. The `server/research/index.ts` mismatch already existed at the previously reviewed core 61853e2, where it hashed to `5b9f683b` against the `b8db03cf` pin. It is not new in this delta.
3. The authors already disclosed the hold: `docs/health-launch/HL17_ACCESS_HUB_20261001.md:38-40` and the ADP03 handoff (sole failing test `:387`). The underlying `static.ts` and `App.tsx` edits remove a single redirect line each.

None of this removes the hard `fileHashes` failure on `server/static.ts`. That alone makes the mandatory gate exit 1 at 8f24082.

verdict.reasoning:
The facts in the finding hold up, but the governance harm it describes cannot happen at this SHA. The change is held behind the protection gate until the owner decides, so what is left is a disclosure gap in the request that will go to the owner.

What I confirmed:
- The approved IA lists `/research/access-hub -> /` as a 301 (af5713863:docs/ux/xenios-clarity-program/04_INFORMATION_ARCHITECTURE.md:131).
- B-1 lets protected files change "only to implement the owner-approved clarity information architecture", and every such change still needs protected-change review (af57138:19_FINAL_OWNER_APPROVAL_RECORD.md:36-46).
- cfdfd4e added both redirects: server/static.ts diff line 20 and the App.tsx Route at diff line 186. PROTECTED_CHANGE_REVIEW.md:5,22,35 covers them under B-1.
- 0d22757 removes exactly those two lines.
- HL17_ACCESS_HUB_20261001.md calls itself a "restoration" (line 1) and never mentions B-1, the clarity IA, or IA:131 (lines 1-56). The original HL-17 correction was "point these links to the real ordering entry, or remove them" (e7b74feb:01_FINDINGS_c213707.md:338). HL-17 instead brought back a page the IA had retired.
- The alternative fix the finding proposes is almost entirely inside the allowed zone. Every live link site is under client/src/research/. The one link in a protected file, client/src/lib/nav.ts:75 (nav.ts is a permitted seam in the manifest), is the `accountEntry` export, and nothing imports it. So that fix would need no protected change.

Why this is not P2:
1. The change is explicitly held, not quietly ratified. HL17 doc:40 says "Previous owner approvals do not cover this successor", that the manifest is unchanged, and that "Any mismatch is a release hold, not an authorized baseline amendment." The task scope at .xenios/ACTIVE_TASKS.json:22 requires "unchanged manifest and held hard static baseline until separately approved amendment". HL17 doc:3 says "Not approved for release."
2. The gate actually enforces this at HEAD. The manifest still pins server/static.ts to sha256 9cd3e1c3... as a hard hash (CORE_SITE_PROTECTION_MANIFEST.json:703) and App.tsx to 3b3b808b... in seamBaselineHashes (line 1254). At 8f24082 the LF-normalized files hash to 1bc59371... (App.tsx) and b7a76417... (static.ts). Both checks in verify-core-site-protection.mjs:302-303 therefore fail, and so does server/core-site-protection.test.ts:320/386.
3. Building first and getting the owner's exact-hash approval afterwards is the established procedure, not a bypass. The precedent is 663268f, docs/phase2/HEALTH_PROTECTED_HASH_APPROVAL_20261001.md. The missing owner decision is a pending step that the records list as open: PROJECT_STATE.json:163 has "two protected seam reviews/owner amendments", and the HL11 handoff at line 288 says HL-17 "needs the protected routing/nav ownership and review".

What remains is P3. When the owner is asked to amend the two hashes, the request does not say that it reverses an approved B-1/IA:131 redirect, and it does not offer the allowed-zone option. The owner could approve without knowing they are overriding their own IA decision. The fix is to cite IA:131 and B-1 in HL17 doc:38-48 and ask for an explicit choice: supersede IA:131, or revert the two lines and repoint the Research links. That matches part of the proposed correction.

Two citation notes:
- af57138 is not an ancestor of HEAD; the clarity-program docs live only on claude/xenios-clarity-spec-20260926. The B-1 lineage still reaches HEAD through cfdfd4e (an ancestor) and the manifest's App.tsx seam note at line 371 ("register the B-1 public clarity routes and redirects").
- The cited HL17:20-23 covers cold-focus and search policy, not the restoration framing. The relevant lines are 1, 18 and 40.

verdict.reasoning:
I checked the mechanism and it holds. The severity does not.

What I confirmed at 8f24082:
- 88's preflight refuses with ASSISTED_ORDER_EFFECTS_ADOPTION_REQUIRED when the outbox has no assisted_order_verification_id column and any row matches template_key='research.assisted_order.status_changed.customer' with payload->>'status'='paid' (supabase/migrations/20261001040351_research_assisted_order_quote_effects.sql:27-35). The check ignores the row's delivery status, so notices that were already sent also block it.
- The live runtime 79414143 can produce exactly that row:
  - Production is 79414143 per docs/coordination/CURRENT_PRODUCTION_STATE.json:64,520, and that file records 'assisted order bridge mounted' and 'outbox worker started'.
  - The runtime allows payment_review->paid (79414143:server/research/assisted-order/service.ts:94).
  - Its only evidence check is a free-form paymentVerificationId (service.ts:197). The M71 set_status RPC accepts the same move (79414143:supabase/migrations/20260815150000_research_assisted_order_bridge.sql:904,925).
  - On every status change it enqueues templateKey research.assisted_order.status_changed.customer with payload.status=updated.status (service.ts:846-862), through enqueueNotificationOnce into research_notification_outbox (production-deps.ts:149-156; outbox.ts:83-86).
- research-notification-outbox.sql has no delete or retention path.
- The pre-80 preflight never reads the outbox (supabase/verification/research_assisted_order_quote_pre80_preflight.sql:9-34). Its NO-GO rule covers only nonterminal frozen rows (MIGRATIONS.md:428). verdict.reasoning:
This is Class B (should fix before launch), so P2. The finding is not Class A / P1.

What I confirmed at d1da288:

- **Foliage counts.** I looked at the contact sheet and at 01, 21, 22, 23 and 24 at full size. Real leaves or plants appear in 01–21 and 25, which is 22 of 25. Image 22 has a palm-frond shadow and 23 has a leafy shadow. Image 24 has neither.
- **Unrequested slabs.** Travertine-style slabs appear in product-form classes that never asked for stone (04, 05, 08–11, 13, 15, 16, 18).
